evidence.title: Authors report task-specific compressed communication conventions emerging under character pressure and postmortem discussion, with some transfer to weaker newcomer agents.
evidence.observation: Authors report task-specific compressed communication conventions emerging under character pressure and postmortem discussion, with some transfer to weaker newcomer agents.
evidence.evidence_standing: Bounded observation (author-reported study; not independently reproduced)
evidence.glossary_fit: Bounded comparison; no change to definitions and no universal claim
evidence.limitations: Simulated scenario; character budget is not measured human intervention latency. Low-pressure agents remained closer to English, and high-pressure agents often failed even with postmortems. English perplexity is a proxy, not proof of malicious concealment or universal human incomprehensibility.
evidence.open_questions: Generality, independent replication or formal validation beyond the inspected scope remain open.

terms.name: Cross-system feedback
terms.definition: A pattern in which an action or output from one technical or organizational process affects activity elsewhere and subsequent responses modify conditions for additional participants. Many response paths may exist; there need not be a single linear loop.

terms.name: Observability boundary
terms.definition: The practical limit of what a given observer or monitoring arrangement can detect, interpret, or causally connect. The limit may be known, partly understood, or itself unrecognized.
